rows.why: The printed cell diagram was transcribed as a set-apart [Diagram: ...] block naming what each of the five leader arrows rests on (coiled ribbon membranes, a small shaded body with a dark dot, the large lobed body), which is enough to land on option C.
A [Diagram: ...] block states that bob R hangs lowest and P and T hang highest, which is the only fact the potential-energy comparison needs.
A parenthetical block describes all four printed cells (A and C budding, B undivided, D constricted into a figure-of-eight), so the binary-fission choice is readable from the text.
A parenthetical block describes slides I-IV, naming slide I as rounded yeast cells with an attached bud and II-IV as amoeboid cells, which decides the answer.
A parenthetical block names all four steps (boiling water, iodine, ethanol in a water bath, room-temperature water), which is everything the sequencing needs.
The transcription describes only figures I, II and III and says a step IV is 'referred to in the options' without describing it, so option B (I, II and IV) cannot be evaluated against anything.
The prose gives both the covered middle band of figure 1 and the top/middle/bottom colour pattern of all four result diagrams A-D.
The food chain is spelled out (aquatic plants to crustaceans to small fish to large fish) and each option pyramid is described in prose in both the stem block and the option text.
The stem points at four drawn Lewis structures but each option states its bond order in words, so the triple-bonded N2 option is pickable from chemistry alone.
The four drawn structures are never shown, but each option text spells out ring size, bond pattern and H count, so benzene is identifiable without the figure.
The stem inlines the whole diagram: arrow A is solid to liquid, B liquid to gas, C gas to liquid and D liquid to solid, leaving only the naming of the four changes.
The gas is fixed by the reaction the stem states (metal plus dilute H2SO4 gives H2); the figure only shows the collection apparatus and changes no answer.
All four options are prose statements about electrolytic refining, and the incorrect one (impure anode metal described as pure) is decided by the chemistry, not by anything drawn.

The stem writes out the electron count in each shell of all four drawn atoms (diagram 1 has about one electron in the first shell, diagram 2 about four), which is exactly what the Bohr-model test needs.
A parenthetical block states that the plotted straight line is v = u at 45 degrees meeting the u-v curve at P, which is all the geometry the (2f, 2f) answer rests on.
The stem names the whole set-up in words (lamp, slide MN, lens, screen), and real-magnified-inverted follows from the slide-projector arrangement without reading any drawn distance.
Candle, lens and screen are all named in the stem and the answer turns only on the image of a distant object forming at the focus, so no drawn distance is read off.
The prose says which of the four students' incoming rays are parallel and where each converges, naming D as the single sharp point on a correctly placed screen.
The stem states, for each of W, X, Y and Z, whether the protractor's straight edge lies along the mirror or along the normal and whether it sits near the incident or the reflected ray.
Each of the four traced slab paths A-D is written out, including that B alone emerges parallel to the incident ray with a lateral shift.
The incident ray is stated to be parallel to the principal axis and each of (a)-(d) is described by where its reflected ray crosses the axis.
The stem states the incident ray passes through the near-side focus and describes all four emergent rays, so the one parallel to the principal axis is readable.
Both candidate diagrams are described (A gives an inverted image on the far-side screen, B an erect one), which together with parallel rays from a distant tree settles the convex-lens-and-A answer.
The stem states the current direction (east to west, in the plane of the paper), which is the only input the right-hand rule needs; the figure supplies no quantity.
The given trace is written out (amplitude 2 m, two cycles) and so is every option waveform, so softer-at-the-same-frequency resolves to the amplitude-1 two-cycle option.
The given wave (5 cm, period 6 s) and all four option waveforms are described, including the one that keeps the period but changes waveform shape.
For each of A-D the stem says whether i and r are measured from the wall or from the normal, which is the whole discrimination the question asks for.

The transcription describes set-ups A and C identically (two tubes inclined symmetrically either side of the normal) and B and D identically, yet the key is C alone, so only the printed figure can separate the two.
The stem states that in diagram A both angles are marked to the normal on opposite sides and equal, and that the others are marked from the reflecting surface or on the wrong sides.
Each of (i)-(iv) is described by where its angles are measured from, naming (iv) as the one with i and r to the normal on opposite sides and equal.

The incident pulse (upright, moving toward a rigid wall) and all four option pulses (inverted or upright, near or far from the wall) are written out, which fixes the inverted-pulse-next-to-the-wall answer.
Each option text states the prism's orientation and which face the white beam strikes, so the base-at-top case that puts blue third from the top is identifiable without the drawings.
No figure is involved at all: the rule matched the letters 'in fig' inside 'fig wasp completes its life cycle in fig fruit', on a two-statement assertion item.
The stem is truncated as well as figureless - it names the cycle ABCDA and never says which quantity is asked - and the Zero/Positive/Negative choice depends on the missing loop's sense.
Claim (c), that W from x to z via y equals W from x to y, holds only if the y-to-z leg is isochoric, and the shape of the two paths exists solely in the missing figure.
The three claims are about T1, T2 and T3, and nothing in the stem says which states carry those labels; they exist only on the unattached adiabatic-versus-isothermal P-V plot.
Neither the P-V cycle ABCD nor the four candidate diagrams exists: the options are bare (a) to (d) placeholders, so five separate figures are missing from one row.
Work done round cycle ABCD is the enclosed area, and the stem gives no pressure or volume coordinate for A, B, C or D; the keyed pV comes entirely from the plot.
The keyed 4MR^2 depends on where the R/3 disc is cut out and where O sits relative to it; the stem gives neither, only 'as shown in figure'.
'shown below' points at the LaTeX reaction printed inline on the next line, not at any picture; the row carries everything it needs.
